units.title: The actual Gaussian target under an orthogonal eigenbasis
units.reader_note: Conditions, formula steps and exact Lean open beside the concise claim. The complete private target-moment application is folded at step6.
units.statement: Orthogonal rotation carries the literal diagonal inverse-precision Gaussian exactly to the Gaussian target of the conjugated precision.
assumptions: \(d\in\mathbb N\), \(d\ge2\), and \(\kappa\in\mathbb R\), \(\kappa\ge2\). This is the hard-family law auxiliary; the full lower-bound parameter regime is handled separately.

For paper indices \(i=1,\ldots,d\), \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(\lambda_i=(\kappa+1)/2+(\kappa-1)\cos\theta_i/2\), and \(\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)\). Lean uses the same grid with zero-based Fin d indices.

\(O\in O(d)\) is any fixed real orthogonal matrix, with either determinant sign; \(A=O\Lambda O^\top\). The claim is pointwise in this fixed basis, with no joint or conditional-law assertion for a random basis.

\(\Lambda\) and \(A\) are precision matrices. Their matrix inverses are the covariances in the actual Gaussian constructors. Positive definiteness is supplied internally by the existing admissibility theorem, rather than by an added premise.

notation.text: Actual centered Gaussians on real Euclidean space and the fixed orthogonal coordinate map.
The squared Euclidean norm and its finite inverse-spectrum mean.

steps.title: Use the actual positive precision family
steps.text: Reuse canonical hard-family admissibility at O and at the identity basis. Both precision matrices and their inverse covariances are positive definite, so the actual Gaussian constructors have their intended covariance.
steps.lean:
have hApos : A.PosDef :=
    (AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumAdmissibility.actual_precision_admissible hd hκ O).1
  have hΛpos : Λ.PosDef := by
    have h :=
      (AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumAdmissibility.actual_precision_admissible
        hd hκ (1 : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ)).1
    simpa [Λ, θ] using h

steps.title: Identify the inverse conjugate
steps.text: Orthogonality cancels the two middle factors. The displayed candidate is a left inverse of A, which identifies the actual matrix inverse.
steps.lean:
have hOleft : U.transpose * U = 1 :=
    (Matrix.mem_orthogonalGroup_iff' (n := Fin d) (R := ℝ)).mp O.property
  have hOright : U * U.transpose = 1 :=
    (Matrix.mem_orthogonalGroup_iff (n := Fin d) (R := ℝ)).mp O.property
  have hΛunit : IsUnit Λ.det := (Matrix.isUnit_iff_isUnit_det _).mp hΛpos.isUnit
  have hinv : A⁻¹ = U * Λ⁻¹ * U.transpose := by
    apply Matrix.inv_eq_left_inv
    change (U * Λ⁻¹ * U.transpose) * (U * Λ * U.transpose) = 1
    calc
      _ = U * (Λ⁻¹ * (U.transpose * U) * Λ) * U.transpose := by
        simp only [Matrix.mul_assoc]
      _ = U * (Λ⁻¹ * Λ) * U.transpose := by rw [hOleft, Matrix.mul_one]
      _ = 1 := by
        rw [Matrix.nonsing_inv_mul _ hΛunit, Matrix.mul_one]
        exact hOright

steps.title: Transport the covariance operator
steps.text: Represent the exact matvec by the canonical Euclidean continuous linear map T. Its adjoint represents the transpose matrix; the inverse identity then identifies the transported covariance operator.
steps.lean:
have hstar : T.adjoint = Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) U.transpose := by
    change star (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) U) = _
    rw [← map_star]
    simp only [Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_eq_transpose_of_trivial]
  have hop : T * Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) Λ⁻¹ * T.adjoint =
      Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) A⁻¹ := by
    simp only [hinv, map_mul, hstar, T]

steps.title: Identify the full Gaussian measure
steps.text: A continuous linear image of a Gaussian is Gaussian. Its mean is zero, and its covariance bilinear form agrees with the actual target. Canonical uniqueness of Gaussian measures from mean and covariance gives equality of the full measures.
steps.lean:
change μ.map T = ν
  apply IsGaussian.ext
  · change (∫ x, x ∂μ.map T) = ∫ x, x ∂ν
    rw [ContinuousLinearMap.integral_id_map IsGaussian.integrable_id]
    change T (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), x ∂multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) Λ⁻¹) =
      ∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), x ∂multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) A⁻¹
    rw [integral_id_multivariateGaussian, integral_id_multivariateGaussian, map_zero]
  · ext x y
    rw [covarianceBilin_map IsGaussian.memLp_two_id T]
    change covarianceBilin (multivariateGaussian (0 : E) Λ⁻¹) (T.adjoint x) (T.adjoint y) =
      covarianceBilin (multivariateGaussian (0 : E) A⁻¹) x y
    rw [covarianceBilin_multivariateGaussian hΛpos.inv.posSemidef,
      covarianceBilin_multivariateGaussian hApos.inv.posSemidef]
    rw [← Matrix.inner_toEuclideanCLM, ← Matrix.inner_toEuclideanCLM,
      ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left]
    change inner ℝ x ((T * Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) Λ⁻¹ * T.adjoint) y) =
      inner ℝ x (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) A⁻¹ y)
    rw [hop]

steps.title: Use the canonical latent norm moment
steps.text: The private application actually invokes the new law and the existing diagonal Gaussian moment theorem. Its paired API is instantiated at the internally chosen valid frequency 1 to extract the frequency-independent norm component. The orthogonal map is measurable and preserves the norm for every vector.
steps.lean:
have hLaw : μ.map R = ν :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumTargetLaw.actual_rotated_gaussian_target hd hκ O
  have hm :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumGaussianMoments.actual_diagonal_gaussian_quadratic_means
      hd hκ 1 (by decide) (Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 1 < 2) hd)
  have hLint : Integrable g μ := hm.1
  have hmean : (∫ x, g x ∂μ) =
      ∑ i : Fin d, ((κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i))⁻¹ := hm.2.2.1
  have hR : Measurable R :=
    (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin d) (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ)).continuous.measurable
  have hnorm (z : E) : ‖R z‖ = ‖z‖ :=
    ContinuousLinearMap.norm_map_of_mem_unitary
      (Unitary.map_mem (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin d)) O.property) z
  have hg : Continuous g := continuous_norm.pow 2
  have hcomp : g ∘ R = g := by
    funext z
    change ‖R z‖ ^ 2 = ‖z‖ ^ 2
    rw [hnorm]
  have hmapLint : Integrable g (μ.map R) :=
    (integrable_map_measure hg.aestronglyMeasurable hR.aemeasurable).2
      (by rw [hcomp]; exact hLint)

steps.title: Obtain the actual target norm mean
steps.text: Rewrite the target measure using the proved full law. Transport integrability through the measurable map, then evaluate the integral by norm preservation. The complete private Test, including its exact statement and producer call, is folded here.
steps.lean:
import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumTargetLaw
import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumGaussianMoments

open Matrix InnerProductSpace MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped BigOperators
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
Actual target norm-square consumer. The full rotated Gaussian law is genuinely
used to transport canonical diagonal L1 and the finite inverse-spectrum mean.
No moment/law/integrability certificate is an input. This is the norm component,
not all Lemma4.5, a pass probability, algorithm or query/cost assertion.
-/
namespace AutoSamplingTheory.Tests.GaussianComplexityFixedSpectrumTargetLaw

private theorem actual_target_gaussian_norm_mean {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d)
    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 2 ≤ κ) (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) :
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let Λ : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ :=
    Matrix.diagonal (fun i => (κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i))
  let A : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ :=
    (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) * Λ *
      (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ).transpose
  let μ : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :=
    multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) A⁻¹
  Integrable (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) => ‖x‖ ^ 2) μ ∧
    (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), ‖x‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) =
      ∑ i : Fin d, ((κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i))⁻¹
:= by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let Λ : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ :=
    Matrix.diagonal (fun i => (κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i))
  let A : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ :=
    (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) * Λ *
      (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ).transpose
  let μ : Measure E := multivariateGaussian (0 : E) Λ⁻¹
  let ν : Measure E := multivariateGaussian (0 : E) A⁻¹
  let R : E → E := fun z =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 ((O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp z)
  let g : E → ℝ := fun x => ‖x‖ ^ 2
  have hLaw : μ.map R = ν :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumTargetLaw.actual_rotated_gaussian_target hd hκ O
  have hm :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumGaussianMoments.actual_diagonal_gaussian_quadratic_means
      hd hκ 1 (by decide) (Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 1 < 2) hd)
  have hLint : Integrable g μ := hm.1
  have hmean : (∫ x, g x ∂μ) =
      ∑ i : Fin d, ((κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i))⁻¹ := hm.2.2.1
  have hR : Measurable R :=
    (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin d) (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ)).continuous.measurable
  have hnorm (z : E) : ‖R z‖ = ‖z‖ :=
    ContinuousLinearMap.norm_map_of_mem_unitary
      (Unitary.map_mem (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin d)) O.property) z
  have hg : Continuous g := continuous_norm.pow 2
  have hcomp : g ∘ R = g := by
    funext z
    change ‖R z‖ ^ 2 = ‖z‖ ^ 2
    rw [hnorm]
  have hmapLint : Integrable g (μ.map R) :=
    (integrable_map_measure hg.aestronglyMeasurable hR.aemeasurable).2
      (by rw [hcomp]; exact hLint)
  change Integrable g ν ∧ (∫ x, g x ∂ν) = _
  rw [← hLaw]
  refine ⟨hmapLint, ?_⟩
  rw [integral_map hR.aemeasurable hg.aestronglyMeasurable]
  change (∫ x, (g ∘ R) x ∂μ) = _
  rw [hcomp]
  exact hmean

end AutoSamplingTheory.Tests.GaussianComplexityFixedSpectrumTargetLaw

units.dependency_notes: Canonical admissibility is the public law producer parent. Canonical diagonal moments are an additional private application parent; the new law is actually used by that application. These roles do not create a second public Anchor or a duplicate generic Gaussian node.
units.lean_statement: The literal precision family, full real orthogonal matrix and actual Gaussian constructors are expanded in the exact statement. Matrix inverses are covariance parameters; no positive-definiteness, law, moment or measurability certificate is an input.
units.lean_proof: The actual inverse-conjugation identity and canonical Gaussian mean/covariance uniqueness prove the full law. The complete private application derives measurable norm-preserving transport and consumes both the new law and existing latent moments.
units.boundary: This is the fixed-basis Gaussian law and the private target norm-moment component. It supplies no joint Haar or adaptive output law, full Lemma4.5, target test-probability bound, concentration-valid absolute constant, sampling algorithm, oracle/TV/precision/query-cap/cost adapter, or either complete main lower bound. The basis rotation is a mathematical coordinate map with no algorithmic access or cost claim.
